detail.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Makes `cfg.checkpoint` the only source of checkpoint policy for training and inference. `CheckpointConfig` already existed and both containers already carried it; this PR moves its checks and derivations onto the class, builds it through one factory, and switches the consumers (`checkpointing.py`, the training loop, the async worker, initialization, fault tolerance, autoresume, the RL rollout bank, the ModelOpt loader and builder, the inference loader, the legacy finetune loop) from `args` to the section. The call sites that used to rewrite checkpoint arguments around a single load or save (checkpoint conversion, the RL reference-weights load, the distillation teacher, the legacy finetune tasks, the inference entry points forcing `exit_on_missing_checkpoint`) pass the values that differ as arguments of that load or save, or set the inference flag on the section, and write nothing to `args`. A checkpoint records the policy that produced it, and a resume reads that record.

No flag is added, renamed or re-typed; no default changes; the parser is identical to `main`.

## Issue tracking

Part of #3554 (args namespace to config container). Same shape as #7591, #7778, #8149 and #8211; converges on the shape Megatron-Bridge uses for its checkpoint config.

## Design

- **Schema.** The three flags that configured checkpointing without being fields (`--dist-ckpt-workers`, `--override-ckpt-iteration`, `--ckpt-drop-redundant-extra-state`) become fields with the same dests and defaults. `use_dist_ckpt` is a read-only property (`ckpt_format != "torch"`); `args.use_dist_ckpt` keeps being maintained for readers outside this PR. A parser snapshot test pins the checkpointing group to `main` (dests, defaults, `nargs`, choices, actions).
- **Validation on the class.** `CheckpointConfig.validate()` holds the own-section checkpoint rules: the three checks that ran at construction (the `__post_init__` is gone, so constructing the class runs no check) and the checks `validate_args` applied to checkpoint arguments alone; it raises only. It is the one set of checkpoint rules for both frameworks: Megatron-Bridge's subclass runs it from its `finalize()` (see Compatibility). `validate_args` calls `checkpoint_config_from_args(args).validate()` after the entry-point `args_defaults` are applied, so the CLI keeps rejecting the same inputs with the same messages (the call site moved: the migrated rules now run together, right after the defaults loop). The cross-section checks follow the convention of #8796: the containers check them from their own sections (`_validate_checkpoint()` on both; the inference container checks the `torch_dcp` / FSDP2 pairing, the one rule its sections can express), and `validate_args` keeps `main`'s inline checks at `main`'s positions, so every CLI entry point is covered whatever container it builds and the Gloo rule runs after `use_distributed_optimizer` is rewritten, as on `main`.
- **Derivations at finalize.** The four flips `validate_args` applies (`exit_on_missing_checkpoint` for a conversion, `async_save` without a persistent worker under a distributed format, `replication_jump` without replication, `load_optim` under `--skip-train`) run inline in the containers' `_finalize()` (the first three through `_derive_checkpoint_policy()`, shared by both containers; the `skip_train` rule in the training container), with the legacy conditions and a warning only when a value changes; `validate_args` keeps its flips, so a CLI run finalizes silently. `set_global_variables` finalizes inference containers too (the checkpoint converters never reach `initialize_megatron`), and `pretrain()` finalizes the registered container before fault-tolerance setup, which captures the save directory and the async mode.
- **One factory.** `checkpoint_config_from_args(args)` replaces the two inline copies; it folds the `--no-*` aliases and the `ckpt_fully_parallel_*` dests and accepts a sparse or Python-built namespace. `project_checkpoint_policy(args, checkpoint, **overrides)` is its inverse for every spelling of the aliased fields (round-trip tested) and builds the arguments a checkpoint persists, with the values of a conversion save in place of the section's.
- **Consumers read the owner; a load or save names what it changes.** `load_checkpoint` takes `load_dir`, `finetune`, `load_optim`, `load_rng` and `ckpt_format` as keyword arguments and `save_checkpoint` takes `save`, `ckpt_format` and `verify_integrity`; omitted means the run's section. The values are resolved into locals and each helper receives the value it reads next to the run-wide section (the base loaders, `generate_state_dict`, the sharded-metadata builder, the GPT-to-hybrid optimizer decision, the argument check, the save's finalize functions); no copy of the section is composed and nothing writes it. `load_dir=None` clears the directory so the pretrained-checkpoint fallback runs (RL's reference weights rely on that classification, which with `--allow-llm-only-checkpoint` adds the LLM-only load metadata); a string names another directory (the distillation teacher). The two derivations `load_checkpoint` applied to `args` in place (the pretrained fallback's `finetune`, `--freeze-all-layers`' `finetune` and `override_ckpt_iteration`) stay local to the load; the primary load records its outcome on the train state (`TrainState.effective_finetune`, not checkpointed, written only by the load `setup_model_and_optimizer` performs through `record_finetune=True`), and the multimodal dataloader resume reads it, with the checkpoint section, instead of `args.finetune`, `args.pretrained_checkpoint` and `args.load`.
- **MSC.** `enable_msc` is a field; the saver reads it from the section. One helper, `setup_multi_storage_client(enable_msc)`, applies the policy to the process-wide flag (enable; disable so a process does not inherit it from an earlier run; fail early when requested without the package; warn once), called by `parse_args` as before and by `initialize_runtime_services` from the section for every entry point, before the tokenizer or any checkpoint path is read, so a native container gets the same early setup as a CLI run. The `--enable-msc` flag keeps its argparse group next to the deprecated `--disable-msc`.
- **Startup, before any container.** Two readers run before a run config exists and build their policy from the arguments: `load_args_from_checkpoint` (`--use-checkpoint-args`) and the ModelOpt auto-detection (`maybe_enable_modelopt`, which decides the model config class the entry point builds; its run-time fallback callers pass the registered section).
- **Persisted policy.** `state_dict['args']` is a copy of the arguments whose checkpoint names are projected from the effective section (byte-identical to the former saved arguments for a CLI run, conversion included), and the saved run config's `checkpoint` section is the effective one. On load, the saved checkpoint section is read right after the rank-0 pass and decides what the checkpoint holds (optimizer state, for the load template and the GLU guard alike; RNG state; the legacy optimizer sharding); the saved arguments remain the fallback for checkpoints written before the run config was saved with them, and for the `args`-less checkpoints Megatron-Bridge writes the section is the only source.
- **Inference.** The same factory, consumers and checks; `InferenceConfigContainer` gets a `_finalize()`; `get_model_for_inference`, the text generation server, the VLM dynamic server and the checkpoint converters set `exit_on_missing_checkpoint` on the section before their load (their policy decision; nothing else in the inference container's twenty-odd other users changes).

## Compatibility

- The parser is identical to `main` (snapshot test over the 64 actions of the checkpointing group).
- `run_config.yaml` gains the three promoted keys under `checkpoint`; a file saved before them loads with their defaults. A checkpoint written by a conversion now records the format and the directory it was written in (`main` recorded the source run's).
- `state_dict['args']` is unchanged for a CLI run, with one documented case: after a pretrained-checkpoint fallback or a `--freeze-all-layers` load, the persisted `finetune` and `override_ckpt_iteration` carry the run's policy (the projection follows the registered section), where `main` persisted the values the load had derived; nothing reads them back from a checkpoint. `load_checkpoint` no longer writes `args.finetune` or `args.override_ckpt_iteration`: the one in-tree reader that needed the effective value after the load, `examples/multimodal/dataloader_resume.py`, reads `TrainState.effective_finetune`; an out-of-tree reader of `args.finetune` after a load sees the run's flag.
- `CheckpointConfig(...)` constructs without checks; code that relied on the constructor to reject `async_strategy`, the nvrx requirement or `verify_integrity` calls `validate()`.
- A save directory without a periodic interval is accepted: `--save` with no `--save-interval` (or `--save-interval 0`) saves at the end of training and on the exit paths only, which is how Megatron-Bridge already reads it. `main` rejected it only because the end-of-training save computed `iteration % save_interval` unguarded; every other save site already treated a falsy interval as "no periodic saves". A negative interval is rejected; `save_retain_interval` requires a positive interval and may not be combined with `most_recent_k` (Bridge's rule, adopted). The retention and `load_main_params_from_ckpt` messages take Bridge's wording, so the shared rule has one message.
- `checkpointing.py` helpers take the value they read, keyword-only where a positional existed: `_load_base_checkpoint(..., *, checkpoint=None, finetune=None)` (the section for the parse-time load), `_load_non_persistent_base_checkpoint` and `_load_global_dist_base_checkpoint` (`checkpoint=`), `_build_sharded_state_dict_metadata(dp_cp_group=None, *, ckpt_format=None)` (no namespace: the optimizer flags come from `cfg.optimizer`, the checkpoint settings from the section), `generate_state_dict(..., *, ckpt_format=None, save=None, verify_integrity=None)`, `check_checkpoint_args(..., ckpt_format=None)`, `_maybe_setup_gpt_to_hybrid_load(..., *, load_optim, saved_save_optim)`; `load_checkpoint(..., *, restore_training_state=False, record_finetune=False, load_dir=_UNSET, finetune=None, load_optim=None, load_rng=None, ckpt_format=None)` and `save_checkpoint(..., *, save=None, ckpt_format=None, verify_integrity=None)`; `get_load_checkpoint_path_by_args` is replaced by `_get_load_checkpoint_path(load_dir, checkpoint)`; `has_modelopt_state(path, *, checkpoint)` and `maybe_enable_modelopt(args, checkpoint=None)`; `TrainState.effective_finetune` (not serialized); `megatron.training.utils.setup_multi_storage_client`. Megatron-Bridge imports `save_tokenizer_assets` only, whose signature is unchanged.
- The two legacy `torch` branches of the ModelOpt loader called `_load_base_checkpoint` without `args` and unpacked three of its four results; they are repaired in passing.
- Megatron-Bridge: its `CheckpointConfig(MTrainCheckpointConfig)` keeps working; the removed `__post_init__` means the three construction checks stop running for Bridge's subclass until its bump PR ends its `finalize()` with `super().validate()`, after the Bridge-only checks. With the save-interval rule above settled on Bridge's reading, the inherited `validate()` accepts everything Bridge accepts; Bridge drops its own copies of the retention and `load_main_params_from_ckpt` rules and its retention tests expect the inherited assertions (the change is prepared on a Bridge branch and verified below).

## Commits

1. `refactor(training): promote the three checkpoint-only flags to CheckpointConfig fields`
2. `refactor(training): CheckpointConfig validates itself; one factory for both containers`
3. `refactor(training): checkpointing.py reads the checkpoint section of the operation`
4. `refactor(training): the remaining checkpoint consumers read cfg.checkpoint; swap sites pass overrides`
5. `test(training): checkpoint consumers follow the section; a checkpoint records and reads its policy`
6. `fix(training): startup ModelOpt detection, projection of sparse namespaces, GLU guard policy` (the three findings of the implementation review: the startup detection read the registered section before one existed, the projection lost a canonical-only boolean, the GLU guard read the saved arguments where the load template read the saved section; regression tests for each)
7. `refactor(training): one checkpoint validate() for both frameworks; a save without an interval is valid` (the `validate_format_prerequisites()` hook that let Bridge skip the rest of `validate()` is gone; the one rule the frameworks disagreed on is harmonized on Bridge's reading, with the end-of-training save guarded; retention and `load_main_params_from_ckpt` messages unified)
8. `test(training): sync the checkpoint section before the setup load in the GLU and MoE numerics tests` (the two CI unit-test failures: fixtures that built the run config before choosing the save and load directories)
9. `fix(training): review 1: CLI cross-section checks for every entry point, legacy finetune flags, autoresume save` (the first review's four findings: the inference and converter CLI paths had lost the `fsdp_dtensor` / Megatron FSDP error, one `save_interval` read through `get_args()`, the derived `finetune` / `override_ckpt_iteration` flags written back to the namespace for readers outside `checkpointing.py`, and the pre-existing autoresume save call missing its FLOP-count argument)
10. `refactor(training): fold the checkpoint cross-section rules into the containers` (second review: #8796's convention; `validate_run()` and `finalize_checkpoint_config()` removed; `_validate_checkpoint()` on both containers, the derivations inline in `_finalize()`; `validate_args` keeps `main`'s inline checks at `main`'s positions, which also restores the Gloo-check ordering tdene found)
11. `refactor(training): pass the per-call load and save choices as explicit arguments` (the `checkpoint=` override, its allowlists and the resolver removed; keyword arguments on `load_checkpoint` and `save_checkpoint`, locals passed to the helpers; the inference entry points set the exit flag on the section)
12. `refactor(training): record the finetune classification on the train state, not the namespace` (`TrainState.effective_finetune`, written by the primary load; the multimodal dataloader reads the train state and the section; the two `args` writes removed)
13. `refactor(training): enable_msc is a checkpoint setting, applied once for every entry point`
14. `test(training): behavioural checkpoint ownership tests only` (the AST scan, the source-order check and the `__post_init__` assertion replaced by behavioural tests)

Then a merge of `main` (`90f4d5279`: the OptimizerConfig migration #8213, the data section #8341, the RL factor-out #4264 among others). Where the two migrations met: `checkpointing.py` reads the optimizer flags from `cfg.optimizer` and the checkpoint settings from the section; the RL reference-weights load, now in `megatron/rl/training_setup.py`, passes `load_dir=None, finetune=True, load_optim=False` and `load_optim=False` for the reload instead of writing `args`; `--skip-train` is evaluation-only for RL too, as #4264 made it in `validate_args`, so the container's `skip_train` rule has no RL exception.
15. `refactor(training): the sharded-metadata builder reads nothing from the namespace` (its `args` parameter was dead after the merge)
16. `fix(training): exempt layer-wise optimizers from legacy checkpoint Gloo rule` and `fix(multimodal): read online evaluation save paths from checkpoint config` (cuichenx, 2026-11-02: the container's Gloo rule applies to the standard distributed optimizer only, as the CLI check does after the emerging-optimizer rewrite; the multimodal example's online-evaluation callbacks read `get_run_config().checkpoint.save`)
17. a second merge of `main` (`01fa4164c`; one conflict, #8844's cached progress-log reader takes the section's save directory) and `test(data): the multimodal provider tests register the run config the provider reads` (the CI failure of the data bucket: the provider tests stubbed `args` and the train state but not the run config the provider now reads)

## Test evidence

Two RTX A6000, `mlm-workstation:26.08-py3`, baseline `main` at the PR's merge base (`ed9c2c8c1` for the first series, `a71470918` after the second review) versus the PR head, same commands on both trees, compared per complete test id and outcome. Counts are per rank (both ranks run the same selection).

- **New tests, 126 cases:** the parser snapshot (4), the ownership module (`test_checkpoint_ownership.py`, 102: CLI/native equality, the factory/projection round trip for every spelling of the aliased fields, every moved check raising the same message from `cfg.validate()` and from `validate_args`, the containers' cross-section checks and inline derivations (once, with their legacy conditions, silent on repeat), the CLI Gloo check after the `use_distributed_optimizer` rewrite, the async finalizer, the lazy async queue and autoresume driven with the namespace stripped of every checkpoint name and with every name set against the section, the persistent-worker start and the resume load through the section, fault-tolerance setup observing the finalized async policy through `pretrain()`, the MSC policy applied by the CLI and by the runtime services and failing early without the package), the checkpointing module (15: a save under a contradicting namespace lands where the section says with the persisted arguments describing that policy, a resume follows the saved section and falls back to the saved arguments only when the section is missing, the GLU guard and the load template agree on the saved optimizer presence, the pretrained-checkpoint fallback makes the load weights-only without writing the namespace, the load directory omitted / cleared / named, the cleared directory keeping the LLM-only load metadata, the primary load recording `TrainState.effective_finetune` while the auxiliary loads leave it alone, the frozen-layer load at both data positions), the run-config save with explicit values (1), the ModelOpt startup detection (4); the multimodal dataloader predicate's tests read the train state. The conversion and inference swap sites are covered by existing tests adapted to assert the keyword arguments and the section flag, and that neither `args` nor the registered section is written by a load or a save.
- **Unit suites, baseline-relative** (`test_checkpointing.py`, `training/`, `test_training.py`, `test_argument_utils.py`, `test_save_run_config.py`, `test_run_config.py`, `test_save_train_state.py`, `test_eval_batch_size.py`, `inference/test_inference_shards.py`, `post_training/`, `data/test_multimodal_dataloader_resume.py`; the baseline is the merge base `a71470918`): 1765 test ids on the PR versus 1639 on `main`; the 1639 common ids have the same outcome, and the 5 failing on both (three `mamba-ssm` imports, one four-rank test, one `uvicorn` import) the same first error line; the 126 PR-only ids are the new tests, all passing (per rank: 1760 passed, 2 failed, 3 errors on the PR; 1634, 2, 3 on `main`). `tests/unit_tests/dist_checkpointing/` at the same heads: 1019 ids on both trees, the same outcome on every one and the same first error line on the 797 failing on both (eight-GPU layouts, `mamba-ssm`, `emerging-optimizers`); per rank 222 passed, 702 failed, 95 errors on both trees. That suite is a baseline-relative result in a two-GPU environment, not a green run; CI's eight-GPU jobs are the coverage for those cases. The RL test modules do not collect in this image (`uvicorn` missing), so the one-line rollout-bank change is covered by CI only.
- **Corpus parity** (the 298 functional `model_config.yaml`): 284 parse and validate on both trees with an identical namespace, and on all 284 the section the PR's factory builds equals the section `main`'s inline block built from the same namespace (plus the four fields the PR adds, carrying the parsed values); the 71 `--use-checkpoint-args` cases run the parse-time restore identically on both trees; the 14 that fail validation fail identically on both.
- **Functional, two GPUs, mock data, `main` tree versus PR tree**, 41 runs: 31 metric-line comparisons identical over their whole windows (baseline repeatability; uninterrupted run; save/resume; async save with the persistent worker; global non-persistent save and resume; `--finetune`; the pretrained-checkpoint fallback, equal to `--finetune`; conversion to `torch` and resume from the converted checkpoint; retention; `--override-ckpt-iteration`; `--no-load-optim`; cross-revision resumes in both directions from a saved and from a converted checkpoint); the missing-checkpoint exit and the legacy async failure exit non-zero with identical messages; the 14 checkpoint directory listings identical; dynamic inference on a saved checkpoint, directly and through `--use-checkpoint-args --ckpt-step`, generates identical tokens; every `run_config.yaml` identical apart from the four keys the PR adds under `checkpoint` (and the format and directory the converted checkpoint was written in); the persisted arguments identical on every checkpoint except `finetune` after the pretrained fallback (`main` wrote `args.finetune`; the PR writes nothing and projects the run's value), the documented case. `--override-ckpt-iteration` does not reproduce the uninterrupted run on either tree (pre-existing: the directory's `latest_train_state.pt` carries the later scheduler state); the dynamic inference example needs a tokenizer with a BOS id on either tree, so those two runs use a tiny offline HuggingFace tokenizer. One further scenario for the harmonized rule: `--save` without `--save-interval` is rejected by `main` at parse time and accepted by the PR, which writes exactly one checkpoint, at iteration 20, with every metric identical to the uninterrupted run.
- **Megatron-Bridge** (`origin/main` `afcc7eee4` in a worktree, its checkpoint suites, compared by complete test id and outcome): against this PR with Bridge unchanged, 0 differing of 1082 ids; with the bump change applied (`finalize()` ending in `super().validate()`, its duplicated rules dropped, its retention tests expecting the inherited assertions; Bridge `main` at `033ca6f65`, this branch after its merge of `main`), the 1414 common ids keep their outcome and the 5 new Bridge tests pass. Explicit cases with the change: Bridge's `finalize()` rejects `async_strategy="other"`, `verify_integrity=True` with `torch` and a negative `save_interval` through the inherited rules, and accepts a save directory with `save_interval` `None` and `0`. After the second review, the bump branch against the merge base `a71470918` and against this head: 1419 ids, 1405 keep their outcome, the 14 that differ fail on the merge base and pass here (the bump branch's tests of the rules it inherits); the 285 failures common to both trees are Bridge `main`'s config suites against a Megatron-LM `main` past Bridge's pin, unrelated to this PR.
- **Lint:** black, isort and ruff over the changed files under `tests/` (the `tools/autoformat.sh` set; pylint ignores `tests/`), `tools/check_copyright.py`, isort on every edited file.

+"""The checkpointing arguments are unchanged while CheckpointConfig becomes their owner.
+
+``legacy_checkpoint_arguments.json`` is a snapshot of the argparse actions of the "checkpointing"
+group at Megatron-LM commit ed9c2c8c1: option strings, dest, default, nargs, type, choices, action
+class, required and const.
+"""
+
+import json
+from argparse import ArgumentParser
+from dataclasses import fields
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+from megatron.training import arguments
+from megatron.training.config import CheckpointConfig
+
+LEGACY = json.loads((Path(__file__).parent / "legacy_checkpoint_arguments.json").read_text())
+
+PROMOTED = ("dist_ckpt_workers", "override_ckpt_iteration", "ckpt_drop_redundant_extra_state")
+DEPRECATED = (
+    "use_dist_ckpt_deprecated",
+    "dist_ckpt_format_deprecated",
+    "ckpt_fully_parallel_save_deprecated",
+)
+
+
+def _full_parser():
+    parser = ArgumentParser()
+    arguments.add_megatron_arguments(parser)
+    return parser
+
+
+def _checkpointing_actions(parser):
+    (group,) = [group for group in parser._action_groups if group.title == "checkpointing"]
+    actions = {}
+    for action in group._group_actions:
+        assert action.dest not in actions, f"{action.dest} is registered twice"
+        actions[action.dest] = action
+    return actions
+
+
+def _describe(action):
+    return dict(
+        option_strings=list(action.option_strings),
+        default=action.default,
+        nargs=action.nargs,
+        type=None if action.type is None else getattr(action.type, "__name__", repr(action.type)),
+        choices=None if action.choices is None else list(action.choices),
+        action=type(action).__name__,
+        required=action.required,
+        const=action.const,
+    )
+
+
+def test_every_legacy_checkpoint_argument_is_unchanged():
+    actions = _checkpointing_actions(_full_parser())
+    assert set(actions) == set(LEGACY)
+    for dest, legacy in LEGACY.items():
+        assert _describe(actions[dest]) == legacy, dest
+
+
+def test_full_parser_has_no_duplicate_option_strings():
+    seen = {}
+    for action in _full_parser()._actions:
+        for option in action.option_strings:
+            assert option not in seen, option
+            seen[option] = action.dest
+
+
+def test_promoted_flags_are_fields_with_their_legacy_defaults():
+    config_fields = {item.name: item for item in fields(CheckpointConfig)}
+    for dest in PROMOTED:
+        assert config_fields[dest].default == LEGACY[dest]["default"], dest
+    for dest in DEPRECATED:
+        assert dest not in config_fields, dest
+    assert "use_dist_ckpt" not in config_fields
+
+
+def test_use_dist_ckpt_is_derived_from_the_format():
+    assert CheckpointConfig().use_dist_ckpt is True
+    assert CheckpointConfig(ckpt_format="torch").use_dist_ckpt is False
+    for ckpt_format in ("torch_dist", "torch_dcp", "fsdp_dtensor"):
+        assert CheckpointConfig(ckpt_format=ckpt_format).use_dist_ckpt is True
+    with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
+        CheckpointConfig().use_dist_ckpt = False

+    """The parsed namespace with every checkpoint-owned name set against the section."""
+    for item in fields(CheckpointConfig):
+        value = getattr(checkpoint, item.name)
+        if isinstance(value, bool):
+            setattr(args, item.name, not value)
+        elif isinstance(value, str) or value is None:
+            setattr(args, item.name, "/contradiction")
+        elif isinstance(value, int):
+            setattr(args, item.name, value + 7)
+    for name in ("save_optim", "save_rng", "load_optim", "load_rng"):
+        setattr(args, f"no_{name}", getattr(checkpoint, name))
+    args.ckpt_fully_parallel_save = not checkpoint.fully_parallel_save
+    args.ckpt_fully_parallel_load = not checkpoint.fully_parallel_load
+    args.use_dist_ckpt = not checkpoint.use_dist_ckpt
+    return args

reviews.body: One remaining migration gap: `examples/multimodal/train.py` still reads `args.save` in `run_online_eval` and `write_online_eval_to_tensorboard` (lines 530, 555–556). Although this is an example script, these functions are passed to `pretrain()` as the `non_loss_data_func` and `process_non_loss_data_func` callbacks, so they run downstream of the training loop. Can we switch these three reads to `get_run_config().checkpoint.save` too?

There's a lot going on in this PR I think. Overall it makes sense. Some higher level concerns I want to have a quick discussion about before merging:

new explicit args to load/save_checkpoint (save_dir, load_dir, finetune, load_optim, etc.). allows changing save behavior/policy without mutating any globals
- concern here is if we need a more general solution, this only supports certain explicit kwargs right now


mirroring/projecting config back to args during save; and restoring checkpoint-related args/config during load
- current logic seems specific to checkpoint 'policy', and also painful to maintain. but i also think we need a more general solution.
